answer: Defining your own bean of the same type; auto-configuration backs off via @ConditionalOnMissingBean.

description: A REST endpoint returns 200 OK for every outcome, including validation failures and missing resources. Clients must parse the body to tell success from failure. How would you redesign the error handling, and what status codes would you use for validation failure, missing resource, and successful creation?
solution: Centralise error handling in a @ControllerAdvice that returns a consistent JSON error body (code + message + field errors for validation). Use 400 for validation failures, 404 for a missing resource, 201 with a Location header for successful creation, and 200 only for successful reads. Return DTOs, not entities, and validate with @Valid at the boundary.
title: Redesigning REST error handling

description: A service loads 100 orders, then accesses each order's line items in a loop, and the database log shows 101 queries. Diagnose the problem and propose a fix that does not make every association eager.
solution: This is the N+1 problem: 1 query for orders plus 1 lazy query per order for line items. Fix it with a JOIN FETCH query, an @EntityGraph, or a DTO projection that fetches orders and items together. Do not switch associations to EAGER, which would load items even when they are not needed.
title: Diagnosing 101 queries for 100 orders
